doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Moving from New York to Los Angeles
summary: Visits before the move, the Sheraton Universal and Carson's joke, and the hotel month provided.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: What was it like moving from New York to L.A.? Were you glad that happened at the time?

I like them both as long as it’s one or the other. But it was easy. They, when we used to come out to visit before we moved here, we’d come out for two or three weeks a couple of times a year. And this was before the Sheraton Universal Hotel was even built. So we used to have to stay way down in Hollywood at what is now the Hyatt on Sunset. In those days it was called Gene Autrey’s Continental Hotel, and we had to drive. Now that’s in the late 60s. About 70, the Sheraton Universal got built so we’d stay there, it was a mile from Burbank. And in return for our staying there, they would plug them on the Tonight Show every night. Carson called it the “Sheraton Unusual Hotel.” So when we moved out from New York they gave us, nobody knew where they were going to live yet or anything, so they just gave us a month and said, “Here, you’ve got the hotel for a month.” So that made it — it simplified things.
